newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Europe, U.S. won't clash over Mideast peace- Dutch.
newsitem.headline: Europe, U.S. won't clash over Mideast peace- Dutch.

text.p: European Union attempts to mediate peace in the Middle East are unlikely to clash with U.S. efforts as both sides of the Atlantic are cooperating closely, Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo said on Monday.
Asked if there was a danger that EU mediation in the Middle East could clash with U.S. diplomacy, Van Mierlo told a news conference: "Everything is possible. But it's not likely."

"(U.S. peace envoy) Mr Dennis Ross and (EU envoy) Mr Miguel Angel Moratinos are cooperating very, very well and are in constant touch. They both play an important role in what is going on today," he added.
"There are sometimes different views and sometimes different interests. But you don't solve it by running away from it. You discuss it and try to find a common approach," Van Mierlo said.
"At this very moment we (EU and U.S.) are very productive and cooperative in the Middle East," he added.
Van Mierlo was visiting Lisbon as part of a tour of European capitals to outline the aims of the Dutch presidency of the EU.

Last October the EU named Moratinos, a Spanish diplomat, as its special envoy to the Middle East with a mandate to observe the peace process, establish relations with Israeli and Palestinian negotiators and report on possible action the EU might take.
